units.title: Domain A: Basics of Food Processing & Preservation

outcomes.text: Define food, food technology, processing, preservation, production and spoilage.
Describe chemical, physical, biological and biochemical spoilage.
Discuss how food is produced and how it spoils.
Assess national and international food security.
Explain preservation principles: keeping microbes out, slowing or killing them, stopping autolysis, inactivating enzymes, and limiting chemical and physical damage.

units.title: Domain B: Techniques of Food Processing & Preservation

outcomes.text: Describe the history of food processing and preservation.
List and explain conventional methods such as drying, curing, blanching, smoking, pasteurization, freezing, fermentation, canning and pickling.

units.title: Domain C: Value Added Food Products

outcomes.text: Define value addition and value added food products.
Discuss value addition of food commodities, with examples like juice, jam, bread and ketchup.

units.title: Domain D: Dimensions of Food Processing & Preservation

outcomes.text: Describe how high, low, chilling and freezing temperatures work in preservation.
Define moisture and explain how it affects shelf life and how water is removed.
List and define drying methods: sun, dehydrating, oven and dehydrofreezing.
Define chemical additives and tell contaminants, adulterants and preservatives apart.
Describe the role of chemical additives.

units.title: Domain A: Basics of Food Processing & Preservation

outcomes.text: Describe food components and sort foods by component, shelf life, pH and source.
Explain preliminary operations such as cleaning, sorting, peeling, size reduction, mixing and filtering.
Describe innovations like microwave heating, high-pressure processing, smart packaging and natural preservatives.
Assess future needs: cutting food waste, freeze drying, and cheap eco-friendly preservation.

units.title: Domain B: Techniques of Food Processing & Preservation

outcomes.text: List and describe novel thermal techniques: ohmic, microwave, radio frequency and infrared heating.
List novel non-thermal techniques: high pressure, pulsed electric fields, ionizing radiation and ultrasonication.

units.title: Domain C: Value Added Food Products

outcomes.text: Define value addition and explain why processing and preservation matter for these products.
Apply conventional processing and preservation methods to make value added products.
Explain how juices, jams, breads, cakes, sauces and similar products are made.
Describe the industrial and economic importance of value added products.

units.title: Domain D: Dimensions of Food Processing & Preservation

outcomes.text: Tell preservative from non-preservative chemical additives.
Explain the roles of preservatives, nutritive additives, sweeteners, flavors and colors.
Describe food laws on chemical additives.
Define fermentation.
List fermented foods.
Discuss organisms used in fermentation, such as probiotics, bacteria and fungi.
Describe fermentation's benefits: better digestion, immunity and nutrient availability.

units.title: Domain E: Food Packaging & Food Industry

outcomes.text: Define food packaging and food labeling.
Describe why packaging and labeling matter to industry and consumers.
Explain what makes a good packaging material: affordable, easy, safe and eco-friendly.
Identify packaging materials such as paper, board, plastic, glass, cans and tetra pack.
